ground_truth.description: If the token used by the LockManager can be flashloaned (or flashminted) and a proposal is created with the voting mode EarlyExecution, anyone could be able to 'early execute' it by flashloaning tokens, locking them, casting a YES vote to trigger early execution, unlocking tokens, and repaying the flashloan - all in one transaction. The vulnerable code is in LockToVotePlugin.vote() at lines 205-207 which calls _attemptEarlyExecution() when VotingMode.EarlyExecution is set.
ground_truth.root_cause: If the token used by the LockManager can be flashloaned (or flashminted) and a proposal is created with the voting mode EarlyExecution, anyone could be able to 'early execute' it by flashloaning tokens, locking them, casting a YES vote to trigger early execution, unlocking tokens, and repaying the flashloan - all in one transaction. The vulnerable code is in LockToVotePlugin.vote() at lines 205-207 which calls _attemptEarlyExecution() when VotingMode.EarlyExecution is set.
ground_truth.attack_scenario:
1. Flashloan the needed amount.
2. Lock the flashloaned amount via LockManager.lock().
3. Cast a 'YES' vote via LockManager.vote() which triggers LockToVotePlugin._attemptEarlyExecution().
4. Proposal executes immediately in same transaction.
5. Unlock the tokens via LockManager.unlock().
6. Repay the flashloan.
ground_truth.fix_description: Avoid allowing the early execution in the very same block that the vote has been made. This would require tracking the 'success' of a proposal in a separate flag, stored in the proposal struct. Alternatively, remove the EarlyExecution voting mode entirely.

vulnerabilities.type: flash-loan governance takeover (early execution without balance snapshot)
vulnerabilities.explanation:
When a proposal uses VotingMode.EarlyExecution, LockToVotePlugin.vote() immediately calls _attemptEarlyExecution() in the same transaction after updating the tally. Voting power is derived from the caller-provided _newVotingPower (passed by LockManager as the user’s current locked balance) and there is no snapshotting or minimum lock duration.

As a result, if the underlying governance token is flashloanable/flashmintable, an attacker can temporarily acquire a large balance, lock it, vote YES to satisfy _canExecute(), and trigger execution immediately. Because execution happens before the attacker unlocks and repays the flashloan (all within one tx), the protocol treats transient voting power as if it were durable governance power.

This does not require compromising any admin/owner key. The attacker only needs public access to LockManager’s lock/vote functions and the existence of an EarlyExecution proposal whose actions benefit the attacker (or, if proposal creation is permissioned to tokenholders, they may also be able to create such a proposal using transient power depending on DAO permission conditions).
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario:
Preconditions: (1) there exists an active proposal P with parameters.votingMode == EarlyExecution, and (2) the governance token can be flashloaned/flashminted, and (3) the LockManager is authorized to call vote() (normal setup), and LockManager has (directly or via DAO permissions) the ability to execute proposals once they pass.

Steps (single transaction):
1) Flashloan N governance tokens.
2) Approve LockManager to transfer N tokens.
3) Call LockManager.lockAndVote(P, VoteOption.Yes, N) (or lock(N) then vote(P, Yes)). This causes LockManager to call plugin.vote(P, attacker, Yes, N).
4) vote() updates proposal_.tally.yes by N and (because votingMode is EarlyExecution) calls _attemptEarlyExecution().
5) _attemptEarlyExecution() sees _canExecute(P) == true and calls _execute(P), executing the proposal actions immediately.
6) Call LockManager.unlock() to retrieve N tokens.
7) Repay the flashloan. The proposal remains executed even though the attacker no longer holds/locks tokens.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix:
Do not allow execution in the same block/transaction as a vote that causes the proposal to become executable.

Concrete options:
1) Add a per-proposal “passedAtBlock” / “isSuccessful” flag set when thresholds are met, and require execution to occur only in a later block (e.g., require block.number > passedAtBlock).
2) Snapshot voting power at proposal start (or at vote time with snapshot block = block.number-1) so flashloaned balances in the execution transaction cannot be used.
3) Enforce a minimum lock duration (tokens must be locked before proposal start, or at least for X blocks) for voting power to count.
4) Remove/disable VotingMode.EarlyExecution entirely if instant execution is not strictly required.

prediction.overall_explanation: LockToVotePlugin’s EarlyExecution mode enables same-transaction vote-and-execute without any voting power snapshot or lock-duration requirement. If the governance token is flashloanable/flashmintable, an attacker can borrow tokens, lock, vote YES to meet execution thresholds, trigger immediate execution, then unlock and repay within one transaction. This can lead to unauthorized execution of proposals (e.g., treasury-draining actions) using only transient voting power.
